newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CONSUMER CONFIDENCE FELL IN OCTOBER - SF. [Corrected 13:45 gmt]
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CONSUMER CONFIDENCE FELL IN OCTOBER - SF. [Corrected 13:45 gmt]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to show consumer confidence fell, rather than rose).
Finnish consumer confidence fell to 12 points in October from 14.2 in September, Statistics Finland said in a statement on Thursday.

Consumer confidence is measured as the average of respondents' estimates on five variables: One's own finances in the past year and the coming one, the Finnish economy in the past and the coming year, and how advantageous it is to buy durable goods.
In August, the consumer confidence indicator was 12.9 points, in July 10.9, in June 9.8, in May 7.0 and in April 4.5 after falling from 6.1 points in March.
